item.title: Vote for Ames Tribune female Athlete of the Week for Oct. 11-17
item.description: Oct. 11-17 was the final week of the regular season for Iowa high school volleyball and cross country. The girls swimming and diving season is also winding down. In area high school volleyball, Ames defeated Oskaloosa and fell to Class 5A No. 2 Dallas Center-Grimes to end up tied with 5A No. 13 Indianola for third in the Little Hawkeye Conference behind DCG and 4A No. 1 Norwalk. Ballard, the No. 6 team in 4A, downed Gilbert and Bondurant-Farrar to finish atop the Raccoon River Conference and the Bombers also went 5-0 at the Knoxville Invitational. Roland-Story, the No. 10 team in 3A, finished second to 2A No. 7 Woodward-Granger in the Heart of Iowa Conference after sweeping Nevada to finish 8-1 in the conference. All area girls cross country teams competed in their conference meets during the week. Ames ran at the LHC meet in Oskaloosa, Ballard and Gilbert ran at the RRC meet in Alleman and Nevada and Roland-Story competed in the HOIC meet at Perry. Collins-Maxwell and Colo-NESCO ran at the Iowa Star Conference meet in Waverly. There were several standout performances by high school female athletes from the Ames area during the week. Here are the Ames Tribune female Athlete of the Week nominees for the week of Oct. 11-17. AmesTrib.com readers vote to determine the winner, who will be announced at the end of the week. Jayden Peters, Collins-Maxwell Peters won the Iowa Alliance Conference varsity girls individual championship at the IAC cross country meet on Oct. 13 at the Wartburg Max cross country course in Waverly. Peters completed the 5-kilometer course in 19 minutes, 15 seconds flat to beat Colo-NESCO's Hayden Hendrick by 23.7 seconds for the title. Addison Lynch, Ames Lynch turned in a tremendous individual match for the Ames volleyball team during the Little Cyclones' 25-23, 25-17, 25-20 sweep of Oskaloosa in LHC play on Oct. 13 at Ames. Lynch handed out 26 assists for the Little Cyclones. She also had 10 digs, seven kills and one ace. Harper Weig, Nevada Weig turned in a top-three performance for the Nevada girls cross country team during the HOIC meet on Oct. 12 at Perry. Weig ran a 5k time of 20:22.6 to trail only West Marshall's Dalaney Eldridge (20:05.8) and Woodward-Granger's Chlover Wall (20:15.8). Addison Hosteng, Ballard Hosteng had a fantastic performance for the 4A No. 6 Ballard volleyball team during the Bombers' thrilling 18-25, 25-20, 25-20, 24-26, 15-12 win over No. 15 Bondurant-Farrar in a RRC match on Oct. 15 at Bondurant. Hosteng led Ballard with 19 digs, went a perfect 19 of 19 serving with three aces and tallied two blocks. She was also a weapon on offense, finishing with six kills. Miley Geise, Roland-Story Geise turned in another fantastic match at setter to help the 3A No. 10 Roland-Story volleyball team defeat Nevada by scores of 25-18, 25-13, 25-18 on Oct. 15 at Nevada. item.title: Keys to ALCS Game Six for the Guardians
item.description: CLEVELAND, OH - OCTOBER 17: Chase DeLauter #24 of the Cleveland Guardians is seen in the dugout during Game Four of the American League Championship Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field on Saturday, October 17, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Rob Tringali/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Just make sure you get to keep playing baseball, boys. The Guardians continue to have somewhat of a snake-bitten season at home this season, dropping two games against the Rays to head back to Tampa Bay down 3-2 in a 7-game series. They now face Freddy Peralta for a second time, who threw six scoreless against Cleveland in game 2 (after also dominating the Yankees in the ALDS). Meanwhile, the Guardians will open with the “reliable vet” option of Shawn Armstrong and the rest of their pitching plan for the game being, essentially, a shaken 8-ball reading “Reply hazy, try again.” Keys to Game Six for the Guardians: 1. Hit Freddy Peralta’s Fastball : Peralta is a three-pitch pitcher with a four-seamer, a changeup, and a curveball. Peralta threw a season-high 71% four-seamer mix against the Guardians in game two of the ALCS. It worked. So, does that mean he goes back to the same plan in an “if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it” philosophy, or does he make an adjustment to mix in more changeups? Peralta’s average velocity on his fastball was up 2.6 mph from his season average, so I suspect he is simply going to let this pitch ride and dare the Guardians to hit it. We have seen enough of the Rays’ pen to know that there is a reason they haven’t lost a game this season when leading after eight innings. They are very good, so they need to find a way to get to Peralta to have a chance tonight. So… there you go, Guardians. Gird your loins, hit the fastball, and this has a good shot of going to a winner-take-all. For what it’s worth, during the season, Chase DeLauter was 15 runs above average against the fastball, Steven Kwan 5.2 runs above average, Travis Bazzana 4.5 runs above average, and Brayan Rocchio 2.1 runs above average. 2. Adjust to Playing on Turf : There were a couple rough plays on the Tampa Bay turf in games one and two and the Guardians’ defense has been shaky the past two nights. If the Guardians win tonight, they will need to play clean defense and adjust to the various quirks of the turf at Tropicana Field. 3. Strategically Deploy Your Pitchers : After Armstrong, I think we will be set to see Daniel Espino, Joey Cantillo and Tanner Bibee in some capacity. Foster Griffin threw 44 pitches on Saturday… so he could also get an inning, given the elimination game dynamic. Stephen Vogt will need to leverage these arms in the right moments to have a chance at turning the game over to his high leverage arms (who also all threw yesterday, of course). The Guardians continue to have somewhat of a snake-bitten season at home this season, dropping two games against the Rays to head back to Tampa Bay down 3-2 in a 7-game series. They now face Freddy Peralta for a second time, who threw six scoreless against Cleveland in game 2 (after also dominating the Yankees in the ALDS). Meanwhile, the Guardians will open with the “reliable vet” option of Shawn Armstrong and the rest of their pitching plan for the game being, essentially, a shaken 8-ball reading “Reply hazy, try again.” Keys to Game Six for the Guardians: 1. Hit Freddy Peralta’s Fastball : Peralta is a three-pitch pitcher with a four-seamer, a changeup, and a curveball. Peralta threw a season-high 71% four-seamer mix against the Guardians in game two of the ALCS. It worked. So, does that mean he goes back to the same plan in an “if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it” philosophy, or does he make an adjustment to mix in more changeups? Peralta’s average velocity on his fastball was up 2.6 mph from his season average, so I suspect he is simply going to let this pitch ride and dare the Guardians to hit it. We have seen enough of the Rays’ pen to know that there is a reason they haven’t lost a game this season when leading after eight innings. They are very good, so they need to find a way to get to Peralta to have a chance tonight. So… there you go, Guardians. Gird your loins, hit the fastball, and this has a good shot of going to a winner-take-all. For what it’s worth, during the season, Chase DeLauter was 15 runs above average against the fastball, Steven Kwan 5.2 runs above average, Travis Bazzana 4.5 runs above average, and Brayan Rocchio 2.1 runs above average. 2. Adjust to Playing on Turf : There were a couple rough plays on the Tampa Bay turf in games one and two and the Guardians’ defense has been shaky the past two nights. If the Guardians win tonight, they will need to play clean defense and adjust to the various quirks of the turf at Tropicana Field. 3. Strategically Deploy Your Pitchers : After Armstrong, I think we will be set to see Daniel Espino, Joey Cantillo and Tanner Bibee in some capacity. Foster Griffin threw 44 pitches on Saturday… so he could also get an inning, given the elimination game dynamic. Stephen Vogt will need to leverage these arms in the right moments to have a chance at turning the game over to his high leverage arms (who also all threw yesterday, of course). The one thing I definitely would like to see is Espino facing a different part of the order than Diaz and Caminero who have seen him quite a bit. You know, I feel so good about this Guardians’ season. I will be disappointed in a loss because you can never guarantee yourself this kind of opportunity again, but I also feel proud of what these guys have done to get to this point. I would be so sad because there is a good chance I will not see any more Guardians’ baseball until at least Memorial Day, but I have a lot of happy memories from 2026 to keep me warm. I also would be happy to watch the Brewers-Rays World Series because I like both teams and would enjoy seeing either get a title. But, hey, neither of them deserve to see one as much as Cleveland baseball fans do. None of their players deserve a ring like Jose Ramirez does. So, let’s see our guys really fight to keep this ride going another day.

item.title: Sergio Perez: Debut Cadillac season "without a doubt one of my best years"
item.description: Motorsport photo If one looks at Sergio Perez's numbers in the 2026 Formula 1 season, the campaign could be classified as disastrous. So far, Cadillac has not scored a point, although the Mexican came close to achieving it at the Monaco Grand Prix where he took the MAC-10 up to tenth position before suffering a penalty. But while the numbers tell part of the story, one must look at the full picture, which is not always reflected in the final standings. For instance, the performance in Baku can't be forgotten where, from the very first day, he was close to placing in the top 10. Nor can Singapore be overlooked, where he was close to building a lap's advantage over his teammate Valtteri Bottas —situations that the results table does not show. In an exclusive interview with Motorsport.com, Perez was asked if he would consider 2026 as his worst season, to which he was direct: "No, not at all. "In terms of results, obviously, but I think people who understand the sport can see the level at which I am driving and the level I've been maintaining, the performance I've delivered, and they can understand the caliber of the year I've had." Until now, in every single year he had competed, he had scored points, from his debut with Sauber in 2011 to his final campaign with Red Bull in 2024. Now, that possibility seems distant with six races remaining to conclude the campaign. But for Perez, it is important to look at all the elements surrounding this debut year, where for the first time he has had to lead and build a project from scratch with a car that has undergone various modifications since the first race to resolve reliability issues, up to now, where he himself has become the leader of the team, steering the development and, when the tools have allowed, competing against the midfield. Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing "In the end, Formula 1 depends heavily on your car to achieve big things," he said. "Ultimately, we have people who know a lot about this sport, and obviously my team, and they know the level I'm at." When asked where he would place 2026 within his career compared to other seasons, evaluating his results and performance with the car he has had, he stated: "I think one of my best years. Without a doubt, in terms of confidence, driving level, decision-making, leadership, without a doubt one of my best years. "I am being part of something so important and fundamental in a new project. My voice carries a lot of weight here, and I think that, as a driver, carries a lot of responsibility as well." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

Calvert-Lewin (left) remained standing while other players took the knee before Sunday's match between Leeds United and Manchester United [Getty Images] Announcing this month's campaign, the Premier League said: "Players will be taking the knee before kick-off during the next two match rounds to show unity against all forms of discrimination." Kick It Out told BBC Sport that taking the knee "still has value in raising awareness" but that they "understand the reasons players might become frustrated with the pace of change". Between 2021-22 and 2025-26, reports of both discrimination and racism received by the charity more than doubled, and reached record levels last season. High-profile cases have also highlighted the continuing abuse faced by players. After England defender Jess Carter received racist abuse online during last summer's Women's Euros, the Lionesses stopped taking the knee. "Taking the knee, that's not enough. We have done that for a while. The impact is not good enough, it's not as big as we think," said England manager Sarina Wiegman at the time. The No Room For Racism campaign extends beyond taking the knee. "We are using the reach of our players to send an important message: we are united in the fight against racism," said Premier League chief executive Richard Masters. Players have also helped develop educational resources about diversity, available to more than 19,000 primary schools across England and Wales. "I think it's important for young people to see role models who look like them, to see that they can achieve anything. It doesn't matter who you are, what you do or how you look," said Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk as part of the campaign. "It means a lot to me to represent my community on and off the pitch." item.title: Chris Boswell Makes Steelers History in Week 6 Win Against Buccaneers
item.description: Chris Boswell Makes Steelers History in Week 6 Win Against Buccaneers originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Since joining the team in 2015, Chris Boswell has been one of the most reliable members of the Steelers . He proved that by making history in the Steelers’ Week 6 win against the Buccaneers. item.title: Manchester City suffer injury blow as Enzo Maresca confirms Erling Haaland availability
item.description: Enzo Maresca's Manchester City will return to UEFA Champions League action on Wednesday -Credit:James Gill - Danehouse, Getty Images Enzo Maresca has confirmed that Erling Haaland is fit to face AEK Athens — but Manchester City teammate Antoine Semenyo will be sidelined for approximately eight weeks. City striker Haaland was spotted limping at the conclusion of Saturday's thrilling 3-2 victory over Ipswich Town. Prior to the win, Maresca revealed he may be forced to drop the 26-year-old from his starting lineup to prevent injury. But Haaland wasn't the sole concern from the Ipswich fixture. Matheus Nunes and Mateo Kovačić both departed injured during the second half, while Semenyo picked up a knock after entering the field as a late substitute. Ahead of City's home match against Athens on Tuesday, Maresca provided an update at a press conference, via The Mirror : "He (Haaland) can be available. We will see. Cristiano Ronaldo delivers brutal Portugal 'ultimatum' after Jorge Jesus 'broke his word' FIFA 'Peace Prize' awarded to Donald Trump may be scrapped amidst Gianni Infantino controversy -Credit:Richard Sellers/Allstar, Getty Images "We have a session now. We have some doubts after Saturday's game. He was quite good yesterday, better. The rest are more or less okay. The only one that will be out for probably eight weeks is Antoine. "In the first moment we expect an even worse injury so we were more worried but after the scan we are less worried. It could be eight weeks. Now the most important thing is to recover it. When he is back, around December, we have a new player. It's not muscular. "To lose Antoine, or any player, is not good. In terms of Erling, we said we can use Antoine as a nine but we have different players to try. We will see, at the moment it is Erling, we don't need to think about another one." Maresca went on to address how players such as Haaland and Semenyo — who featured at the FIFA World Cup — will require careful management. "We need to pay attention to workloads," the City boss continued. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE "That is why we will do some changes tomorrow. Try and keep players fit. Some things are out of our control, like Antoine. "Antoine was one of the players we wanted to rest, he played 10-15 minutes, and then he got injured. We need to pay attention [to the World Cup players]." City return to their Champions League campaign sitting on three points, having defeated FC Porto 2-0 on the road in their opening fixture before suffering a 4-2 defeat against Paris Saint-Germain at the Etihad. Athens are also level on three points, having overcome LASK in their opener before last week's loss to Shakhtar Donetsk.

item.title: 24-Team College Football Playoff Could Alter Postseason Expectations
item.description: MIAMI, FLORIDA - The College Football Playoff National Championship Trophy on display prior to the Head Coaches News Conference at JW Marriott Marquis Miami on January 18, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Leonardo Fernandez/Getty Images) Getty Images Recall the good old days when making a bowl served as a goal to attain? A standard that set some teams far apart from others? When making a bowl saved a coach’s job at least for another season? My, how things have changed. More change will soon be upon the college football postseason picture if “ constructive discussions ” between the CFP and ESPN turn into a 24-team playoff field effective next season. To think five-loss Duke could have made the CFP last season, the second year of the current 12-team playoff structure. The five highest-ranked conference champs made the cut, and the playoff committee did not have to take the ACC champ Blue Devils. This year, each of the power conference champs are admitted to the privileged side of the velvet rope regardless of record. (At least through Week 7, it appears there will be no such mediocrity in a conference championship game. Of course, it would have helped if the ACC helped itself with tiebreakers, etc.) A 24-team field? Not only does it open the door fairly wide for multiple three-loss teams and perhaps a four-loss team (on top of a potential five-loss power conference champ) to attend the party, but a football program’s expectations will likely be realigned. For one, making the CFP might not be the standard. Rather, advancing within the bracket would be. Though being part of a 24-team field would hardly qualify as exclusive company, being among them could be how a coach’s success (or not) is gauged. Losing opening-round games in a field of 24 could have its consequences. After all, there might be teams outside the top 25 that make the cut. For a top 15 program to fall short against a non-ranked or barely ranked foe two years in a row, for example, could light up message boards and the seat of a coach attempting to get his program to move along in the expanded bracket. On the flip side, such an expanded field could purchase time for a coach who rarely has his team in the limelight, but has churned out one pretty good year after another. An example could be North Carolina State’s Dave Doeren, who has not posted even one double-digit win season in 13 years – and looks like 14 – guiding the Wolfpack. Yet, he had 10 winning seasons, including four of the nine-win variety on his resume. Pretty darn good, right? A nine-win campaign could result in a playoff appearance in a 24-team field. Suddenly, there is a celebration in Raleigh. Doeren and the Wolfpack are just an example, but a legitimate one of how a playoff field doubling in size to two dozen could alter the view of a program’s direction and a coach’s tenure. Here are a couple of other things that could result. Big regular season games not nearly as big There were valid concerns that a 12-team playoff would diminish the value of least a handful of late-season games. For the most part, that was not the case as a larger playoff pool meant more meaningful November games as teams scrambled to make the cut. That allowed for some awesome television viewing of games that otherwise might not have generated much of any pregame hype. Doubling the field to 24? Well, many – not all – mid-to-late November clashes would be served with less mustard. After all, a team that could not afford to lose a late-season game might have a mulligan coming to it as a second or even third loss could be easily absorbed without altering the larger picture. Instead of settling for a bowl in front of maybe 15,000 fans at whatever location, a playoff spot could remain firmly within such a team’s grasp. Group of Six bonanza? How about three or four non-power conference teams making the playoff? The highest-ranked Group of Six team is currently guaranteed a spot. Playoff inventory that doubles in size may not filter down to the G6 when it comes to number of guaranteed spots. It may remain at one. That said, we saw what happened last year when the Sun Belt’s James Madison and Tulane of the American – JMU is moving to the American in 2028 – made the playoff last season. Two non-power conference teams out of 12 total teams made the cut. Could three or four teams from the G6 enjoy playoff prestige in the larger pool? You bet it can. Power conference teams could cannibalize one another to the point several slip from the top 25 and fade from playoff contention. item.title: Brentford contact police after rugby ball kicked into stadium
item.description: Brentford said matchday safety is of "utmost importance" following the incident during the game against Liverpool [Getty Images] Brentford say they are working with the police following a "dangerous" incident in which a rugby ball was kicked from a height towards the pitch during their Premier League game with Liverpool. A video on social media shows a man standing on a rooftop near the Gtech Community Stadium, kicking a rugby ball towards the pitch while others laugh and cheer. Another clip from inside the ground shows the rugby ball being taken away from the pitch by a member of staff as play continued. In a statement, Brentford, who were beaten 2-1 on Saturday, said "such behaviour is dangerous and potentially very harmful". "The matter has been referred to the police and the club is supporting the relevant authorities in their investigation to help identify those responsible and take appropriate action, which may result in criminal prosecution," the statement added. "The matchday safety of fans, staff, players and officials is of utmost importance, and the club will support all efforts to ensure action is taken." Brentford, who had Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt both sent off in the second half, are sixth in the league table after the defeat. item.title: Flick talks Raphinha, Rodri, De Jong, Kounde, Luis Enrique, Alex Campos ahead of PSG vs Barcelona
item.description: Flick talks Raphinha, Rodri, De Jong, Kounde, Luis Enrique, Alex Campos ahead of PSG vs Barcelona It will be a clash of the heavyweights tomorrow night at Parc des Princes as FC Barcelona lock horns with Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Champions League. The Blaugrana go into the game on the back of an exceptional 11-game winning streak across all competitions this season. PSG, meanwhile, are the best team in Europe, having won the UEFA Champions League for two seasons in a row, setting up a mouthwatering contest. Ahead of the exciting match-up in Paris, Barça manager Hansi Flick spoke to the media, praising his opposite number Luis Enrique, while also discussing Barcelona’s defensive options amidst a spate of injuries. Hailing the job Luis Enrique has done at PSG in recent seasons, Flick remarked: “He won two Champions Leagues in a row. His team plays fantastic football. He’s an excellent coach, one of the best in the world.” “I like their dynamism, their intensity, how they press, how they play and rotate. The players change positions frequently. They’re very flexible. I love it. It’s incredible how this team has evolved. He’s doing a fantastic job.” Flick was full of praise for Luis Enrique’s PSG. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) On how this match is a test for Barcelona and where they stand in Europe, the manager added: “It will be a good test for us to see where we stand. I’d like my team to play with confidence, courage, and together, as we have in recent matches. “We’re playing against arguably the best team in the world over the last two years. It’s a good opportunity to show our level and see what we can improve. After the match, we’ll know a lot.” On injuries and availability Barcelona go into the game without both Jules Kounde and Eric Garcia, while Andreas Christensen is also unavailable. On top of that, Gerard Martin’s availability also remains uncertain. As such, Flick was asked about Barça’s defensive options for the game tomorrow, to which he replied: “We have options. Rodri and Frenkie can play. Àlex Campos is with us; he’s trained with us for the first time. I’m positive. It’s not the best time for us, but we have to accept it.” Providing an update on Kounde’s condition, he offered an optimistic outlook, saying: “Jules will be back soon; maybe he’ll be an option for the weekend. We have to wait and see.” Flick also confirmed that captain and top goalscorer Raphinha is ready to start the game after having returned from an injury over the weekend. “Yes, he can be a starter,” he said. On Barça’s style and PSG’s evolution Barcelona came up short against PSG during last season in the league phase of the Champions League. Discussing what the difference between the team from last year and the current one was, Flick explained: “Last year was difficult. This year, we’ve played from the start with the style we want and expect from the team. We have a lot of confidence on the ball, we create a lot of chances. It’s completely different.

item.title: ‘It makes me sick’: Jon Gruden does not hold back on game-changing referee decision
item.description: USA TODAY Sports The Los Angeles Rams fell in an 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon, dropping to 2-4 on the season, and a controversial personal foul call played a big role in the final seconds. The Rams have plenty of reasons to be frustrated with the officials, but former NFL head coach Jon Gruden is already doing the complaining for them. Gruden blasted the NFL’s replay system on Monday, saying that it “makes me sick” that the call wasn’t corrected. And he questioned why the league even has a replay official if he isn’t going to step in on a call like this one. Controversial Call Against Rams The Rams took a 16-15 lead with 47 seconds left after Matthew Stafford hit tight end Colby Parkinson for a touchdown. But on the Cardinals’ final drive, Jalen Brooks made a 21-yard catch, and Rams cornerback Josh Wallace was flagged for unnecessary roughness after Brooks’ helmet collided with him as he came down with the ball. The penalty added 15 yards to the play and set up Chad Ryland for a 43-yard field goal, his sixth of the game, as time expired. Even the Fox broadcast questioned the call. “It looked, to me, like Brooks is just landing on Wallace’s right shoulder,” analyst Greg Olsen said, via Fox Sports . “For me, that’s one I do not think needs to be called,” added Fox rules analyst Mike Pereira. ‘It Makes Me Sick’ Gruden, who now works with Barstool Sports after resigning as head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders in 2021 amid his email scandal, didn’t hold back during an appearance on Wake Up Barstool on Monday morning. “We have a guy in the booth; he’s called the replay official,” Gruden said, via Awful Announcing . “And his job is to look at the game and see calls that are screwed up. He has communication with the white hat. And I should just say, ‘Hey, Dave, you really screwed up that call, pick up the flag.'” “Now, for that not to happen, it makes me sick. I don’t understand what the hell we’re doing! We have all this technology; look at this super high-speed, Emmy Award-winning shots you’re showing. What’s the point in having a guy up there communicating?” Gruden continued. It’s worth noting that Pereira pointed out that replay could only take the flag off if there was no contact at all. In this case, there was contact, even if it was not worthy of a personal foul. item.title: ‘Always Played the Right Way’ – 2-Time WNBA Champion Hypes Up Gabby Williams as ‘One of the Best Players in the World’
item.description: Oct 9, 2026; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams (1) reacts after defeating the Golden State Valkyries during game three of the second round for the 2026 WNBA Playoffs at Michelob Ultra Arena. © Candice Ward-Imagn Images Gabby Williams has had a career year in her first season with the Golden State Valkyries. She led her squad to the No. 2 seed in the playoffs with a 32-12 regular-season record. Now, the Valkyries find themselves up 1-0 in the WNBA Finals, in large part, thanks to Williams’ excellent two-way production. Kelsey Plum Gives Gabby Williams Her Flowers Kelsey Plum has had a successful WNBA career. The two-time champion in 2022 and 2023 with the Las Vegas Aces has five All-Star selections, made the 2022 All-WNBA First Team, and won Sixth Player of the Year in 2021. She certainly knows a thing or two about winning at the highest level. Plum appeared on the “ Girls Tripp ” podcast hosted by broadcaster Allie Clifton and WNBA insider Jordan Robinson. The veteran star discussed why people should not be surprised by Williams’ 2026 breakout campaign. “WNBA fans are now getting a taste of who Gabby Williams is … Gabby’s been one of the best players in the world for four or five years … In Seattle, she never got the opportunity to iso at the top of the key … It’s awesome to see somebody that has basically just waited her turn but has always played the right way,” Plum said. Williams averaged a career-high 14.4 points with 3.3 rebounds, 2.2 assists, and 1.6 steals in 2026. The advanced numbers certainly back up Plum’s claims regarding Williams taking advantage of her opportunity. According to Basketball Reference , the Golden State forward carried a 29.01% usage rate in the regular season, smashing her previous career high of 21.0% in 2019 with the Chicago Sky. However, Williams is not just an offensive threat. She made the 2026 WNBA All-Defensive First Team and finished second in the Defensive Player of the Year race behind Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese. The Valkyries’ defense was on full display in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals against Atlanta on Saturday. Golden State held the Dream to just 8 points in the fourth quarter to complete a comeback victory. Atlanta shot 2-for-19 from the field and 0-for-7 from beyond the arc in the final frame. Williams helped Golden State contain Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard throughout the game. The two Atlanta stars shot 5-for-19 and 3-for-14 from the field, respectively, as the Valkyries made them work for every bucket. On the other end, Williams carried Golden State, scoring 26 points as the only double-digit scorer in her finals debut. She scored 16 points in the second quarter alone and brought the Valkyries back into the contest after the Dream led 22-14 after the first frame. item.title: Georgia drops in AP Poll after upset loss to Auburn
item.description: The Georgia Bulldogs were lost 27-24 to the Auburn Tigers on Saturday. Georgia went into the game as the No. 1 team in the AP top 25. They had notable wins against Alabama , Vanderbilt, and Oklahoma. Other teams like Texas lost two weeks ago to Oklahoma, which catapulted Georgia to No. 1 ahead of Week 7 in college football. But that ranking wasn’t held very long, and with the loss to Auburn , they’re down four spots and are now ranked 5th. The Miami Hurricanes are now ranked 1st after beating Florida State 43-35 in double overtime. BYU is 2nd after beating Notre Dame. Although the Bulldogs lost, they still are a good team. item.title: Scottie Scheffler, Hideki Matsuyama headline 2026 Hero World Challenge field
item.description: World No. 1 and two-time Hero World Challenge champion Scottie Scheffler and defending champion Hideki Matsuyama were announced on Monday as leading a star-studded field at the 2026 Hero World Challenge. Hosted by Tiger Woods, the 20-man field features seven of the top 10 players in the world, including No. 3 Cameron Young, winner of the Players Championship in March, and No. 4 Matt Fitzpatrick, a three-time Tour winner this season. Japan’s Matsuyama stuffed his approach at the first playoff to set up birdie and defeat Alex Noren to win the Tiger trophy last year. Matsuyama, a two-time winner at Albany in 2016 and 2025, and Scheffler, who won back-to-back titles in 2023 and 2024, are both looking to become the first three-time winner at Albany. Will Tiger Woods play in the 2026 Hero World Challenge? Missing from the announcement was any news about if the tournament host would play. Woods, 50, has often used the 72-hole, no-cut event to mount one of his latest comebacks from injury. Woods hasn't played in an official PGA Tour event since the 2024 British Open at Royal Troon Golf Club, where he missed the cut. He had hinted at potentially playing at the Masters in April but that was before he was arrested on March 27, after an SUV rollover crash on Jupiter Island, Florida, not far from his home, where deputies found hydrocodone pills and noted signs of impairment. He spent time at a rehab facility in Switzerland and has kept a low profile ever since. There has been no indication from his camp when or if he will play again. Hero World Challenge field notables The Hero field currently features 106 combined Tour victories and six golfers who have amassed 11 major championships. Eleven 2026 Presidents Cup participants, including eight from the victorious U.S. team, are in the field. Three players – Si Woo Kim, Ryan Gerard and Jacob Bridgeman – will make their Hero World Challenge debuts. item.title: Jota 'met some demons' during long injury absence
item.description: [SNS] Jota admits he "met some demons" during his long injury absence but believes there is no need to "rush" his return to full match fitness at Celtic. The Portuguese winger, 27, sustained cruciate ligament damage in April 2025 and made his first-team return last weekend in the 2-0 win at Motherwell. And, after coming off the bench again in Sunday's 7-1 Scottish Premiership victory at home to Hearts, Jota believes the ordeal has strengthened his character. "I've met some demons and I've had some good talks with them," he said. "We developed a good relationship and we are all on the same table nowadays and we can laugh about everything that happened. "If you don't grow from a situation like this, it's because you didn't learn anything. "I could step away, see different things from other perspectives and value some stuff that maybe I wasn't valuing before. "I have a clear idea of what I want, what I am. There's no lost time because I grew a lot. It had to be what it had to be and I didn't lose. I actually gained because I'm way stronger nowadays." Hearts roll out red carpet ... and Celtic walk all over it 'Four points is nothing' - O'Neill stays cool after statement win Jota's game time will be restricted to domestic games in the short term as he is not in Celtic's Europa League squad, with Celta Vigo visiting Glasgow on Thursday (20:00 BST). However, he is valuing what playing opportunities he has. "My love for football is immense," he explained. "Maybe someone else wouldn't want to come back because of the struggle or some guys just don't have that in themselves. "That was my fuel to keep on working every day, to be healthy and fit, even if things weren't going that way. "This is my dream. It's my passion. So there's moments where you reflect, there's moments where you're down and you cannot see any light but that doesn't mean that you stop believing. You just need to find another way. "My aim was always to come back fit, whatever time I need to take because I still have a long career in front of me and I'm still young. "So there's no rush, let's do everything correctly and just trust the process." Ron Duguay’s daughter shares an update on his Stage 4 colon cancer battle and asks followers for prayers Duguay wrapped up his hockey career in 1989, recording 274 goals and 346 assists in 864 games. He later spent 12 years covering hockey for MSG Network before his departure in 2018. Now, the former Rangers star’s daughter, Shay Thomas, has shared a black-and-white photo from his hospital room. The photo shows her kissing her father on the forehead as he lies in bed. She wrote, “Thank you to everyone who has reached out and loves our dad so deeply. Your continued prayers, love, and support mean more to our family than you know.” She continued, “As you all know, Dad is a fighter, and he never stops fighting. We’re taking it one day at a time, holding on to our faith, and believing in his healing. Please keep praying for our dad.” Following her post, friends and fans shared supportive messages and prayers. One of them wrote, “Continuing prayers for your dad and for you. God heal Ron and let that healing be a testimony to those who need to believe.” Another commented, “He made such an impact on me growing up. I idolized him. All these prayers are going to help.” Duguay, who helped the New York Rangers reach the 1979 Stanley Cup Final, was diagnosed with Stage 4 colon cancer in December 2024. He kept his diagnosis private until February 2026, when his family shared the news. They also launched a GoFundMe campaign to help cover the costs of his care. Since his diagnosis, he has reportedly undergone surgery to remove his appendix and gallbladder. item.title: ‘Rodri or Frenkie de Jong could play there’ – Hansi Flick offers update on Barcelona’s defensive options ahead of PSG test
item.description: Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images | AFP via Getty Images Hansi Flick is facing quite the selection headache ahead of Barcelona’s Champions League clash with PSG on Tuesday as Jules Kounde and Eric Garcia have been ruled along with Andreas Christensen, leaving the coach with very few defenders available. Gerard Martín is also a doubt and the coach did not want to confirm whether the full-back could start on Tuesday or not, but he did speak about the other options at center-back currently available in the squad. “We have options. Rodri and Frenkie can play [center-back]. Àlex Campos is with us; he’s trained with us for the first time. I’m positive. It’s not the best time for us, but we have to accept it. Jules will be back soon; maybe he’ll be an option for the weekend. We have to wait and see.” It sounds like Martín will be good to go as Pau Cubarsí’s partner, but Flick is more than ready to try something else if Maldini isn’t quite fit enough. Flick’s ability to remain calm when facing these kinds of problems is one of his best qualities as coach, and he will have full trust in whatever back four combination he ends up choosing on Tuesday.

item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
